_note: Hand-written text for the site: the theme of each deck, series or one-off collection (keyed by its id in the MTG repo's tools/site_collections.json), and the inspiration behind each frame. Edit freely; the export script never touches this file. "news" holds an optional line for a batch on the What's new page, keyed by "<date>/<id>" (the date the cards went up and the deck or series id).

magus.tagline: Dressed as a box of old playing cards
intro: I wanted this deck to look like it came out of an old games cabinet. Each frame is based on a real old card, from scans in libraries and museums: Venetian cards engraved in 1748, French story decks from the early 1800s, a Paris fortune-telling deck, a botanical card game, a Marseille tarot and the backs of Victorian playing cards.
Each frame keeps a bit of the original, like the paper colour, the engraved lines or the worn edges. Then the name, cost and rules go where a Magic player expects to find them.

The art is old paintings and engravings. Lands mostly get Romantic landscapes and creatures get natural history plates, with Doré, Turner, Martin and Goya for the big moments. A lot of cards take their colour from the card back, which I re-ink in green, blue or red.
magus.frames_intro: Each of these frames is based on a real old card, cleaned up and fitted to Magic's proportions.

intro: The idea for this deck is a coven of seers, so every card looks like something from their desk: a blueprint, a page lit by a lantern, a table of moons, an almanac. The whole deck is done as cyanotypes, the blue sun prints that 19th-century botanists and engineers used.
It's only black, indigo and Prussian blue, with thin white or grey lines. No gold, no red. It should look like papers that sat in a drawer for a hundred years.

These frames are drawn as clean lines instead of copied from scans, so they stay sharp at any size. The art comes from public museum collections and is all turned into cyanotype, which is how a Rembrandt and a Japanese woodblock print end up the same blue.
truthsayer.frames_intro: Four frames, one for each kind of card: the blueprint, the lantern, the moon and the almanac.

intro: For this one I wanted real occult objects, not horror-film props. Summoning circles in worn gold, sigils scratched into walls, pages from a scorched grimoire, pictures burned onto plaster. It's all black and red, with plenty of grain and soot.
The art is demons and damnation from old manuscripts, Goya, Doré, Blake and the engravers of Hell, printed in red and broken up by the frame as if it had been in a fire.
occult.frames_intro: Five frames, each based on a kind of occult object: a scratched wall, a summoning circle, burned plaster, a branded land and a scorched page.

intro: In Folium the art fills the card and a single leaf lies across the bottom, with the rules written on it. The only decoration is the leaf's veins.

The leaf shape is generated from the card's name, so every card gets a different one. The name is in an italic serif like an old botanical plate, and the leaf is always green, whatever colour the card is.
The art is close-up studies of plants, like Dürer's Great Piece of Turf and Klimt's beech forest.

Portolan is a frame for lands, based on the sea charts sailors used from the 1300s to the 1500s. The art goes all the way to the edge, with the chart lines drawn over it: lines fanning out from a compass rose, and a thin border in the colours of the land's mana.

The middle of the compass rose shows the mana, split into slices for a land that makes more than one colour. The name sits on a small label, and the type line is in red, like the place names on the old charts.
The art is landscapes and harbours by Claude Lorrain, Thomas Cole and Caspar David Friedrich.
Angus is 38 cards I made in one go: mana rocks, counterspells, blue and green staples, and a lot of lands, from fetches and shocks to Strip Mine and City of Brass.

Each card uses one of four simple frames. Fathom puts the bottom of the picture under water. Carrara is white marble with veins in the card's colour. Portolan draws lands as old sea charts. Folium puts a leaf across the bottom of the card.
The art is well-known paintings, like Bruegel's Tower of Babel, Rembrandt's philosopher, Hokusai's Great Wave, Monet's sunrise and van Gogh's almond blossom.
angus.frames_intro: I kept these four frames as simple as I could, so the painting does most of the work.

verdant.tagline: Three frames for a mono-green deck
intro: Three frames for a mono-green deck. The pattern on each card is generated from its name, so they all come out a bit different.
Annulus is the cut end of a log with its growth rings. Contour is a hill map in pale green lines. Rhizome is a slice through the ground, with roots hanging down through the text.
Each frame here copies a technique and generates the pattern for each card. There's paper marbling, Truchet tiles, Turing patterns, stained glass, embossed paper and circle packing.
The patterns are drawn as shapes, not copied from pictures, and each one is generated from the card's name.

layouts.tagline: 17 cards that move the text around
intro: A normal Magic card goes name, picture, type line, rules, top to bottom. Each card in this series does something else.

The text wraps around a circle, spirals out from the picture, runs around the border as one line, or sticks out like sun rays. Some cards are turned sideways or upside down, and one only shows the art inside the letters of the name.
The layouts are done in code, so the text always fits whatever shape it's given.

depth.tagline: Basic lands in front of their mana symbols
intro: Five basic lands done like a magazine cover, where the person on the cover stands in front of the title. Here the title is the land's mana symbol, very big, with a landscape drawn in code in front of it: an oak over the sun, a lighthouse over the drop, a dead tree over the skull, mountains over the flame, spruces over the tree.
Each land comes in three versions: colour, white and black. The colour ones are first, and the white and black ones are under Duplicates.

window.tagline: Basic lands seen through their mana symbols
intro: Five basic lands where the mana symbol is a window. It's cut out of plain paper, very big, and a landscape drawn in code shows through it, fitted to the symbol's shape.
Each land comes in three versions: colour, white and black. The colour ones are first, and the white and black ones are under Duplicates.
Bruegel's Hunters in the Snow (1565) split over three cards. The picture is at the same height on each one, so if you put them in a row you get the whole painting.
Four Islands, each with a different crop of Hokusai's Great Wave off Kanagawa, spaced evenly across the print. Each one is numbered and has a small map of the whole print showing where its crop is.

power.tagline: The Power Nine in one ink each
intro: The nine most famous cards from Alpha, all in the Bitmap frame: big visible pixels and a pixel font, one ink per card.

For each card I cut the main thing out of the original Alpha art, like the jewel on each Mox, the lotus, the figure on Ancestral Recall and the two walkers on Time Walk, and put it on plain paper. The Moxen are one ink per colour, so the five of them make a set.

vesuva.tagline: A lands deck where every kind of card has its own frame
intro: Omo, Queen of Vesuva plays lands, copies lands and turns lands into every land type at once. So instead of one look for the whole deck, I gave each group of cards its own frame, made for what those cards do.

The Urza lands are engineering drawings that join up side by side. The Gates are stone arches, the Loci are a night map with ley lines running from card to card, the search spells are library index cards, and the copy spells show the picture reflected in water. Cards that belong together, like the three waves of the bounce spells or Thespian's Stage and Dark Depths, are made to be laid out in a row.
Every frame is drawn in code rather than copied from a scan. The art is old landscapes and paintings, and Omo herself is a mosaic made from every other picture in the deck.
vesuva.frames_intro: Nineteen frames, one for each group of cards in the deck.

BLEED.name: Bleed
BLEED.text: The art fills the whole card and a real Victorian card back shows only around the edge. The name and rules sit on two paper labels on top of the picture.

STAMPED.name: Stamped
STAMPED.text: Based on a playing card from about 1855. The whole card is a Victorian card back printed in one ink in the card's colour, with the picture and rules set into it.

HYBRID.name: Hybrid
HYBRID.text: The Stamped card back fading into the picture, so the pattern and the painting meet in the middle.

DESTIN.name: Destin
DESTIN.text: Based on Le Livre du destin, a fortune-telling deck printed by Grimaud in Paris in 1865. A tall hand-coloured picture inside a double line, with a small card in the corner for the cost.

TAROT.name: Tarot
TAROT.text: Based on the Tarot Conver of Marseille (1809 to 1833). It has the woodcut double line, a band across the top, and the name in capitals with dots between the words, as in ROY·DE·DENIERS.

FLORE.name: Flore
FLORE.text: Based on the Boston de Flore, a botanical card game from 1820. Engraved lines, a folded-page panel and a chained medallion around the picture, on tinted paper.

FABLE.name: Fable
FABLE.text: Based on French story decks from about 1800 to 1830, like the Grand jeu de Télémaque. A hand-coloured picture, an engraved title ending in a full stop, and a paragraph of script underneath.

VISENTINI.name: Visentini
VISENTINI.text: Based on the teaching cards Antonio Visentini engraved in Venice in 1748. One ink, a header with a diamond-shaped label, the picture, and a centred footer.

HELIO.name: Helio
HELIO.text: A hand-brushed cyanotype sheet with everything drawn in thin white lines, like a blueprint.

GLIM.name: Glim
GLIM.text: Full art lit by a lantern. One patch of the picture is lit and the rest fades into the dark.

SYZYGY.name: Syzygy
SYZYGY.text: For lands. The mana is shown as moons, and a two-colour land is a light and a dark moon in an eclipse.

ALMANAC.name: Almanac
ALMANAC.text: For cards with a lot of text. A table of moons with one row per ability, and loyalty costs shown as light, dark and ringed moons.

SCRAWL.name: Scrawl
SCRAWL.text: Red sigils scratched all over the card, the picture printed in red, the name in rough blackletter and the rules on a soot stain at the bottom.

CINDER.name: Cinder
CINDER.text: A hand-drawn summoning circle in worn gold on burned red-black, with the picture in the middle and sigils around it like a seal.

CHAR.name: Char
CHAR.text: Full art burned onto a wall in red, with soot streaking up from the bottom and the rules written into the soot.

BRAND.name: Brand
BRAND.text: For lands. The picture in dark red behind smoke, with the land's mana burned in like a brand inside a gold ring.

RUBRIC.name: Rubric
RUBRIC.text: The only light frame, for cards with a lot of text. A page from a scorched grimoire, burned at the edges, with the picture printed on the paper.

SIGIL.name: Sigil
SIGIL.text: An early occult frame: the picture inside a lettered seal.

BROADSIDE.name: Broadside
BROADSIDE.text: An early occult frame after printed broadsides and funeral bills.

TABULA.name: Tabula
TABULA.text: An early occult frame for short names.

FOLIUM.name: Folium
FOLIUM.text: The art on top and one leaf across the bottom with the rules on it. The leaf's veins are the only decoration.

PORTOLAN.name: Portolan
PORTOLAN.text: A land drawn as an old sea chart, with lines fanning out from a compass rose that shows the mana, and a border in the land's colours.

KERAMOS.name: Keramos
KERAMOS.text: Based on a Greek black-figure vase from about 530 BC, read from top to bottom: pale clay, black glaze, touches of red and white, and ivy and palmette bands.

MURAQQA.name: Muraqqa
MURAQQA.text: Based on a page from a Persian or Mughal album from about 1600: dyed margins with gold flecks, a blue header and gold lines around the picture.

BAUHAUS.name: Bauhaus
BAUHAUS.text: Based on a 1920s Bauhaus page: one geometric font in lower case, a thick black bar, and Kandinsky's triangle, square and circle at the bottom.

AMOXTLI.name: Amoxtli
AMOXTLI.text: Based on a page from a Mexican folding book from before 1500: white plaster ruled in red, stepped patterns and rows of counting dots.

FATHOM.name: Fathom
FATHOM.text: Full art with no frame. The bottom of the picture is under water, and the text sits on the reflection.

CARRARA.name: Carrara
CARRARA.text: A slab of white marble. The only colour is in the veins, which match the card's colour.

SAMPLER.name: Sampler
SAMPLER.text: A needlework sampler from about 1800. Every stitch is a cross stitch on linen, with a border of red and blue diamonds and the name in a stitched alphabet.

SASHIKO.name: Sashiko
SASHIKO.text: Indigo cloth mended with white running stitch, the way it was done in Edo Japan. The thread is the only decoration, and it makes a stepped pattern around the border.

PAPERCUT.name: Papercut
PAPERCUT.text: A white sheet of cut paper over the card's colour. The name, the cost and the picture window are all holes cut in the sheet.

FAIRISLE.name: Fair Isle
FAIRISLE.text: A Shetland jumper. The whole card is knitted in oatmeal wool, stitch by stitch, with patterned bands at the top and bottom.

ANNULUS.name: Annulus
ANNULUS.text: The cut end of a log, with growth rings across the card. Each log is generated from the card's name.

CONTOUR.name: Contour
CONTOUR.text: A topographic map. The card is hills drawn in pale green contour lines, and every card has its own terrain.

RHIZOME.name: Rhizome
RHIZOME.text: A slice through the ground. The name and picture are above the surface, and roots hang down through dark soil to the bottom.

EBRU.name: Ebru
EBRU.text: Paper marbling done the way a marbler does it: drops of ink pushed outward ring by ring, then combed into tulips.

TRUCHET.name: Truchet
TRUCHET.text: Two-colour Truchet tiles, quarter circles turned according to the card's name, so the colours always meet along the curves.

TURING.name: Turing
TURING.text: A Turing pattern, his model for how spots and coral grow, grown in the border from a seed taken from the name.

LEADED.name: Leaded
LEADED.text: Stained glass. Panes in the picture's colours and some jewel tones, each one shaded, with lead lines between them.

LUMEN.name: Lumen
LUMEN.text: Embossed paper. A pressed border, a sunken edge around the picture, letterpress text and a gold cost.

PEBBLE.name: Pebble
PEBBLE.text: Circle packing. Circles fill the border, biggest first, in the picture's colours, a bit like Kandinsky's circles.

WRAP.name: Wrap
WRAP.text: The picture is a circle in the bottom corner, and the text flows around it.

ORBIT.name: Orbit
ORBIT.text: The picture is a circle. The name curves over it, and the cost sits on a ring around it like beads.

DIAGONAL.name: Diagonal
DIAGONAL.text: One slanted line splits the card, with the picture above, paper below and the name along the line.

SIDEWAYS.name: Sideways
SIDEWAYS.text: The card turned on its side, with a wide picture on one side and the text in a column on the other.

FLOAT.name: Float
FLOAT.text: Full art, with the name, rules and stats on small paper labels on top of the picture, each one just big enough for its words.

UPTURNED.name: Upturned
UPTURNED.text: The card upside down. The rules come first and the name comes last, as big as it fits.

RIBBON.name: Ribbon
RIBBON.text: Full art with the name on a ribbon, the rules on a scroll, and power and toughness on a wax seal.

SPIRAL.name: Spiral
SPIRAL.text: The picture is a circle, and all the text is one line spiralling out around it.

SUNBURST.name: Sunburst
SUNBURST.text: The picture is the sun and the text sticks out from it like rays, one phrase per ray.

ORRERY.name: Orrery
ORRERY.text: The picture is the sun in a model of the solar system, and the text goes around it on tilted orbits.

CALLIGRAM.name: Calligram
CALLIGRAM.text: The rules are set inside the outline of what's in the picture, so the words take its shape.

ANNOTATED.name: Annotated
ANNOTATED.text: Full art laid out like a page in a field guide. Each ability is a note in the margin with a line pointing into the picture.

LETTERFORM.name: Letterform
LETTERFORM.text: The name in huge heavy capitals, with the art showing only inside the letters.

BORDER.name: Border
BORDER.text: No frame and no text box. The art fills the card and one line of text runs around the edge.

BITMAP.name: Bitmap
BITMAP.text: One ink on paper. The picture is made of big visible pixels, and all the text is in a pixel font.

TAP.name: Tap
TAP.text: Upright it reads like a normal card. Tapped, the picture is the right way up and the tap abilities are big.

SPINE.name: Spine
SPINE.text: Made for holding in a fanned-out hand. A coloured strip down the left edge, like a book spine, holds the cost and the name.

DEPTH.name: Depth
DEPTH.text: Like a magazine cover. The land's mana symbol is huge in the back, with a landscape drawn in code in front of it.

WINDOW.name: Window
WINDOW.text: The land's mana symbol is cut out of plain paper, and a landscape drawn in code shows through it.

PANORAMA.name: Panorama
PANORAMA.text: One painting over several cards. The picture is at the same height on each card, so they make one picture when you put them in a row.

SERIES.name: Series
SERIES.text: Each copy of the card is a different crop of the same painting. They're numbered, with a small map of the whole painting showing where each crop is.

MOSAIC.name: Mosaic
MOSAIC.text: Omo's portrait, an ancient bust, made as a photomosaic of every other picture in the deck, each one used about equally, in a gold frame on a night ground.

STRATA.name: Strata
STRATA.text: For the plain mana lands. The picture is the ground surface, with bands of rock underneath in the colours of the mana the land makes, and a key with its land types like a geology chart.

SCHEMATIC.name: Schematic
SCHEMATIC.text: An engineer's drawing on pale drafting film for the Urza lands, with a grid, a line drawing of the land and a title block. Dashed connectors run off the sides, so the four sheets join up in a row.

ARCH.name: Arch
ARCH.text: For the Gates. A stone wall with the picture seen through a gateway, the name carved on the lintel and the mana on the keystone. Each Gate has its own shape of arch.

LEY.name: Ley
LEY.text: A night map for the Loci: the picture in a gold-ringed disc and ley lines leaving the card edges, so the Loci laid side by side join up.

GROTTO.name: Grotto
GROTTO.text: For the Cave lands. You look out of a cave mouth at the picture, with dark rock, stalactites and stalagmites all round.

EVERYTYPE.name: Everytype
EVERYTYPE.text: Full art for Planar Nexus, with a border made of the names of every land type in the rules, running round the card.

DIPTYCH.name: Diptych
DIPTYCH.text: One picture across two cards for the combo pair Thespian's Stage and Dark Depths, with Dark Depths' ten ice counters down its edge.

SCROLL.name: Scroll
SCROLL.text: A hanging scroll on a dark wall for the channel lands, with silk, wooden rollers and a drawn water channel between the two abilities.

LANDFALL.name: Landfall
LANDFALL.text: For the landfall cards. Rings spread out across the picture from the spot where a land lands, then carry on under the rules.

CATALOGUE.name: Catalogue
CATALOGUE.text: For the cards that search for lands: a library index card in a wooden drawer, typed, with a red SEE ALSO line that links the cards in a loop.

FANNED.name: Fanned
FANNED.text: The picture seen through a fan of land cards lying on green felt, as if they were all played in one turn. For the cards that give extra land drops.

MIRROR.name: Mirror
MIRROR.text: For the copy cards. The picture sits above a waterline with its reflection below, and the rules are set on the reflection.

TITAN.name: Titan
TITAN.text: For the big creatures. Near full art with one word of the name huge across the top, and the creature standing in front of its own name.

EXCAVATION.name: Excavation
EXCAVATION.text: A dig section for the graveyard cards: the picture is the surface, and layers of soil run down to dark bedrock where the rules are.

TIDE.name: Tide
TIDE.text: For the three mass bounce spells. The picture goes under a rising sea of breaking waves, higher on each card, so the three show the tide coming in.

SEAL.name: Seal
SEAL.text: For the answers. A dark panel below the picture with a wax seal stamped across the edge, its emblem showing what the card does.

FOLIO.name: Folio
FOLIO.text: For the card draw. The right-hand page of an open book, with the picture as a numbered plate and the rules set as the page's text.

ENGINE.name: Engine
ENGINE.text: Near full art on a dark ground with rounded corners, for the mana rocks and other mana engines.

news.2026-11-26/vesuva: Omo, Queen of Vesuva: a new lands deck, with its own frame for each group of cards.
news.2026-11-25/power: The nine Power cards, all in the Bitmap frame.
